title: 50.6% win rate in backtest, net profit factor 1.63. 4H engulfing strategy on 16 coins, 652 trades,  Deployed on testnet should I make it live?
author: plusaconstant

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I wouldn't go live yet. An 80% annualized return with a Sharpe of 2.4 from a simple engulfing rule is high enough that I'd first look for what flatters it, like stops and targets hit inside the same candle being filled in your favor, or signals using the candle's close before it's known. The 16 coins also move together, so 10 open positions can behave like one big bet in a crash. Compare it against random entries with the same stops and hold time, check the result on a period the rules never saw, and let testnet run a few more weeks to compare real fills against the backtest. If it still holds up, go live with a small size first. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to run those checks against history.

replies.author: plusaconstant
replies.body: It's like when the stop and target are both inside one candle, it counts the stop first. Signals only see closed 4H candles, and a candle that opens past the stop fills at the open, not the stop.The correlation point is real. 16 coins that move together with 10 positions open can act like one big trade in a crash.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Good, counting the stop first and filling gaps at the open covers the main flattering cases. The remaining check is a position cap per correlated group, since a crash day could stop out several coins at once, and then a few weeks on testnet to compare real fills against these assumptions.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Not at 2% risk yet. The rules are simple and you counted fees and slippage, but a few things worry me.

16 coins over the same two years are not 652 independent bets. Most alts move with BTC, so on a hard down day your 10 open positions behave like one big position. 10 x 2% is 20% at risk at once, and the 5% daily stop only stops new entries, it doesn't close the stops that are already sitting there.

The per-coin spread from 39% to 61% is mostly noise at that sample size, so don't drop the weak coins on the strength of it.

Testnet tells you the plumbing works. It doesn't tell you the fills, the testnet book is thin and nothing like the real one.

What I'd do: go live at a quarter of a percent per trade for a month or two, and for every live trade log what the backtest would have filled at on the same bar. If the gap stays near your 7 bps, scale up. If you picked EMA 30, 2.5 ATR and 16 candles after looking at this data, also rerun on a few months it never saw.

replies.author: plusaconstant
replies.body:
Good catch on the daily stop. I checked and it only blocks new entries, the open ones keep their stops. So yes, a bad BTC day could hit most of them at once.   
agree on the per coin numbers too and testnet also. Logging the backtest fill next to the live one is a good idea. Going to rerun it on months it never saw first.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: good that you checked instead of assuming. once the reruns on other months are in, that fill log will tell you fast whether testnet is flattering the entries.
